h: Tszyu Admits He's Rage Baiting Charlo Ahead Of Lara Fight
sum: Tszyu laughs off Charlo's criticism, calls Lara a master of traps, shows interest in Vergil Ortiz and picks Joshua to knock out Fury.
q: So how does how does that make sense that I don't deserve a world title shot?
ctx: Interview with Marcos Villegas of Fight Hub TV
body: Tszyu says he finds Jermell Charlo's constant reactions funny and compares poking him to poking a bear. Asked if he is rage baiting his old rival, he agreed with "Basically, yeah." He says he has nothing against Charlo and gives him respect as a former undisputed champion.

Charlo has said Lara will beat Tszyu and that Tszyu hasn't earned this title shot. Tszyu fired back by asking how he can be undeserving, and said Charlo's call for Lara is “It's just rage bait, man.” He did say Lara is the more technical fighter. A Charlo fight after Lara is possible, he said, but he will sit down with his team first.

On Lara, Tszyu calls it a thinking fight against a very sneaky puncher who sets traps constantly. He expects Lara to come forward, and wants to drag him into deep waters and make it a tough, dirty fight. He also says making 154 had become a nightmare, calls 160 the way to go, and says a fight with Vergil Ortiz definitely interests him. On Fury vs Joshua, he says: “I reckon Joshua by knockout.”
Why it matters: Tszyu is chasing a second division title and already has Charlo and Ortiz in mind as possible next fights. Lara is the test he calls one of the trickiest of his career.

h: Song Jabs Cejudo's Training Ahead Of RAF 15: “I Beat Him Easy”
sum: Song brushes off Cejudo's roast and predicts an easy win in their RAF 15 main event, while Cejudo says he'll show him real wrestling.
q: I think he don't train like he drink every day. I beat him easy.
ctx: RAF 15 press conference in Chicago
body: Henry Cejudo opened the RAF 15 press conference with a long comedy roast of the promotion, its stars and its guests. Then he turned to Song Yadong, the man he faces in the main event.

Cejudo said he still carries a mark from their earlier fight. “I still have a freaking scar on my eye because of it.” He promised to make sure the rules are followed this time and said he gets to show Song what wrestling is. “I get a chance to show him what the sport of wrestling is.”

Song stayed calm. He called it his dream match, said wrestling is the hardest part of MMA, and said he wants to challenge himself in freestyle wrestling. When asked about Cejudo's gold-medal background, he took a shot at Cejudo's preparation and predicted an easy win.

Why it matters: Cejudo is a wrestling gold medalist, but Song already has an MMA win over him. The fight is under wrestling rules, so Song is stepping into Cejudo's world and betting he can still win there.

h: Tsarukyan Calls Out Cejudo And Mocks His Comedy Career
sum: Days before facing Pettis at RAF 15, Tsarukyan says he wants Cejudo next and rips him for leaning into comedy over competing.
q: How Olympic champion can lose to MMA fighter is ridiculous.
ctx: RAF 15 press conference in Chicago
body: Asked at the RAF 15 press conference whether he wanted a piece of Henry Cejudo after his match with Anthony Pettis, Arman Tsarukyan first had to find Cejudo in the room. Once the crowd pointed him out in the front row, Tsarukyan asked him to stand up on a chair so he could see him.
Pressed on whether he really wants to wrestle Cejudo, Tsarukyan didn't hedge. “Of course, I do want to wrestle him,” he said.

He then took shots at Cejudo's career. Tsarukyan claimed that “he's only caring about comedy stuff” and that Cejudo knows he can't wrestle at the same level anymore. He also pointed to a loss Cejudo took to an MMA fighter.

Why it matters: Tsarukyan is the face of RAF and is about to face another former UFC champion in Pettis. Naming Cejudo as his next target gives the promotion a possible follow-up, and it adds to the back-and-forth already building around the card.

h: Odiase Admits He Came In Too Heavy, Eyes 2027 World Title
sum: Odiase beat Perez over ten rounds but says he wasn't at his best. He wants a world title shot by the end of 2027 and hints at a Dubois sparring story.
q: Daniel, keep on winning. You know what happened in sparring. Uh maybe one day the world would know.
ctx: Post-fight interview with Seconds Out
body: Emanuel Odiase won a ten-round points decision over Mike Perez, but he was far from happy with the performance. He says his preparation wasn't where it should have been and that he came in at 122 kg, which he called too heavy. He believes a better camp would have meant the fight didn't go the distance, though he still feels he won every round.

Asked about sparring Daniel Dubois, Odiase wouldn't give details. He said sparring is not the fight, and that he knows he can perform under the bright lights. He told Dubois to keep winning and suggested the world may one day find out what happened in those sessions.

Odiase repeated that 2027 is his year, saying he has said it many times: “2027 world champion”. He said he is ready to fight anyone and that “I know I can beat any man.” He is chasing fighters ranked above him and wants a fight in the first quarter of 2027, then two more before a world title fight at the end of the year. He said he hasn't signed for a possible next fight in his hometown.
Why it matters: Odiase is openly aiming for a world title within a year, and he's pointing at Dubois, a heavyweight champion, while admitting his own preparation has to improve.

h: Garbrandt Says He's Moving On From UFC After 12 Years
sum: Cody Garbrandt says he has nothing left to prove in the UFC and wants more RAF wrestling matches, starting with a possible December 19 date.
q: I've done everything I wanted to do in the UFC.
ctx: RAF 15 press conference in Chicago
body: Asked at the RAF 15 press conference about a rumor that he would retire from MMA in February, Garbrandt didn't confirm it. He said he spent 12 years in the UFC, put on a lot of wars, and is content with what he did there.

He also kept the door open. “I'm not saying that my fighting career is done,” he said, but he added that it's time to move on from the UFC and do something else. He described returning to wrestling as a new love for something lost long ago.

Garbrandt, who faces Sergio Pettis on Saturday, said he wants to keep competing in RAF. He hopes to win and be back on the mats in Long Island on December 19, and says he's in wrestling shape. Of RAF's bosses, he said: “I'll be down.” He also said he'd love to wrestle Henry, whom he called one of the best.
Why it matters: A former UFC champion stepping away from the UFC and into RAF's wrestling format is a notable shift. If he wins Saturday, he could be back in action within weeks.

h: Tsarukyan Says Gaethje Must Drop Belt To Face Volkanovski
sum: Tsarukyan insists he is the next lightweight title challenger and says the UFC told him so, whatever the Gaethje-Volkanovski rumors suggest.
q: And if Gaethje wants to fight Volkanovski, he got to leave the belt and do like a random fight, you know, without the title because I'm contender number one
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting
body: Arman Tsarukyan pushed back on talk that the UFC could book Gaethje against Volkanovski for the lightweight title. Asked if he was worried, he said the next 155-pound title fight is his. He allowed that the promotion might want to do something in a different division, but said he doesn't think so.

He said that if Gaethje wants Volkanovski, he would have to give up the belt and take a non-title fight. Tsarukyan says the UFC told him directly that he is fighting for the title: “the UFC told me that I'm fighting for the belt”.

The interviewer relayed Henry Cejudo's idea of Gaethje vacating to fight Conor McGregor, then Tsarukyan facing Volkanovski for the vacant belt. Tsarukyan wasn't picky about the route or the opponent: “I don't care who is going to be against me”. He named Pettis, Pimblett, Ilia Topuria and Gaethje as possible opponents.

Why it matters: Tsarukyan is publicly staking his claim before anything is official. By his own account, the title fight is likely March or April and isn't confirmed yet, so the UFC's next move at lightweight is still open.

h: Tsarukyan Eyes March Or April Title Shot, Wants Covington Rematch
sum: Tsarukyan expects his UFC title fight in March or April, though nothing is confirmed. He also wants a rematch with Covington and picks Oliveira to beat Lopes.
q: I know I'm can beat him so easy if I'm going to be in the the best shape and I'm going to prepare.
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting's Mike Heck ahead of RAF 15 in Chicago
body: Tsarukyan told MMA Fighting he expects his UFC title fight to come around March or April, but he stressed that nothing is confirmed yet. He said he plans to defend the belt in the summer and again toward the end of next year. He called it the ideal year and described a heavy schedule mixing RAF and UFC fights.

Asked about a rematch with Colby Covington on the RAF mats, Tsarukyan said he is excited. He admitted he didn't gain weight and move up last time, and said he won't take back-to-back wrestling bookings again. He called the jet lag “just excuses” but said he is confident of winning the rematch.

He also picked Charles Oliveira to beat Diego Lopes at UFC 335, saying “it's a decision.” He gave Lopes credit for better boxing and for being young, but said Oliveira is huge for the weight class and has good grappling and conditioning.
Why it matters: Tsarukyan has put a rough date on his title fight and wants a Covington rematch in between. His plans for 2027 are packed, but none of it is confirmed.

h: Song Yadong Wants Dvalishvili Next And Predicts Early Knockout
sum: Song Yadong expects Merab Dvalishvili to be his next opponent and says he can finish him early. He also shrugs off the Usman Nurmagomedov cage incident.
q: I can knock him out. It's like first and second rounds.
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting
body: Song Yadong thinks his next fight will be against Merab Dvalishvili. Asked if that is what's coming, he said he believes it will happen, and that he has heard Dvalishvili say in interviews that he won't fight him.
Song backed it up with a bold prediction. He says nobody has knockout power like his, and that he can end the fight in the first or second round.

The interviewer also asked about the scene after Song knocked out Umar, when Usman Nurmagomedov jumped into the cage and an elbow almost landed. Song laughed it off. He said “It's just wild,” and he doesn't judge it, adding that “he didn't hurt me”.

Why it matters: Song is making a public case for a bout with Dvalishvili while no fight between them is announced. His knockout claim sets up a striker-versus-grappler storyline if the UFC takes it up.

h: Hearn Accuses Dana White Of Mocking British Fans Over Fury-Joshua
sum: Hearn claims Dana White barely promoted Fury-Joshua in America and doesn't want it to succeed because it's staying in the UK.
q: I think Dana White's taking the piss out of the British fans.
ctx: Interview with iFL TV, two weeks before Fury vs Joshua
body: Eddie Hearn went after Dana White in an interview with iFL TV. He said White and Nick Khan are advising on the Fury-Joshua event and that the undercard shows what they are doing. In his words: “They don't know what they're doing.”

Hearn pointed to the late ring time, which he says is aimed at American viewers. He asked who has been promoting the fight in America and said the answer was Dana White, with what he called one post. He claimed they don't want it to succeed because they are annoyed it is still in the UK.

Hearn said he is not involved in promoting the fight, though he has a fighter on the card. He said that if he were running it, the buildup would have been far bigger. “No one drives content like us.” He also said he believes Netflix will overturn the undercard order and move Cordina vs Lara onto the main card.
Why it matters: Fury vs Joshua is two weeks away, and the biggest promoter in British boxing is publicly accusing the UFC boss of undermining the build. That adds a promotional feud to fight week.

h: Sauerland Offers Hearn And White 10 Million Each To Fight
sum: Promoter Kalle Sauerland says he has agreed terms with Eddie Hearn, while Dana White would only do it in a gym. He wants charity money added.
q: So my solution would be you know we'll do it in a gym.
ctx: Interview with iFL TV
body: Kalle Sauerland confirmed he has put 10 million each on the table for Eddie Hearn and Dana White to settle their beef in the ring. The host noted that Hearn had said he is worth more than that. Sauerland brushed it off as Hearn talking.

Sauerland says terms are already agreed with Hearn. He also says he heard White say in an interview that he would like to do it, but in a gym. Sauerland's answer is a gym fight sold on pay-per-view, with money added for charity. He also said a private jet has been thrown in so travel is covered.

The host pointed out that Hearn has not confirmed he would do it for charity. Sauerland said he is sure Hearn does a lot for charity and promised to put his own company's profit into it too. In his words, “we'll add money to charity on it as well.” He pitched it as short rounds rather than a 12-round fight.

Why it matters: The Hearn and White feud has been running for weeks. This is the first concrete offer to settle it, though only Sauerland says Hearn has agreed, and White's gym-only stance is a long way from a signed deal.

h: Hysa Weighs In 15 Pounds Heavier Than Kabayel For WBC Showdown
sum: Both heavyweights have stepped on the scale and faced off for the final time before tomorrow's 12-round WBC title fight in Kabayel's first defense.
ctx: Official weigh-in and final face-off
body: Challenger Nelson Hysa weighed in at 113.2 kg (249.5 lb). Defending WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel came in at 106.4 kg (234.5 lb), so Hysa carries 15 lb more into the ring.

The announcer introduced both men as undefeated. Hysa has 25 wins, 23 by knockout, and holds the WBO global title. Kabayel has 27 wins, 19 by knockout, and is making the first defense of his world title.
The two fighters then faced off for the final time. The fight is scheduled for 12 rounds tomorrow, live worldwide on DAZN, and is promoted by Frank Warren's Queensberry with Gold Star Promotions.
Why it matters: Both men have now weighed in and the face-off is done, so the unbeaten champion and the heavy-handed challenger meet for the WBC title tomorrow, with Hysa the bigger man.

h: Hearn Urges Fans To Push Cordina Onto Fury-Joshua Main Card
sum: Hearn says he was baffled Cordina vs Lara wasn't on the main card and believes fan pressure will force Netflix to move it up.
q: And I believe Netflix will have no choice but to elevate Joe Cordina to the main card.
ctx: Matchroom Boxing video message to fans
body: Eddie Hearn says he was "completely baffled" to learn that Joe Cordina's fight with Mauricio Lara was not on the main portion of the Fury vs Joshua card. He called the matchup a brilliant fight and said giving it main card billing is simple common sense.
Hearn gave two reasons Cordina is on the card at all. One is his own pushing and refusal to give up. The other is “because of the public response and support.”

He is now asking fans to keep the pressure on, repeating what he said on his story: “do your thing, guys.” Hearn says he believes Netflix will have no choice but to move Cordina up, and that they will.
Why it matters: Fans who want Cordina vs Lara on the main card are being told their noise could change the running order. Nothing has been confirmed, and for now Hearn is making a public case.

h: Pettis Says Doubters Will Be Shocked By His Wrestling Debut
sum: Anthony Pettis says no one has seen his wrestling and expects to surprise the people counting him out against Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 15.
q: Might as well go against the champ. If I'm going to go try this for my first time, might as well be against the best right now.
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting ahead of RAF 15
body: Anthony Pettis says he loved the switch-up that put him in a wrestling match with Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 15. He called himself a fan of Tsarukyan and praised the way he is performing in MMA and in wrestling.

Pettis said this is his first wrestling match. He wanted to get his feet wet, but when the Tsarukyan opportunity came up he decided that if he was going to try it, he might as well face the best right now.

Asked about people who think Tsarukyan will go in and run him over, Pettis told them to watch on Saturday. He said “no one's seen my wrestling” and that he has never had to do straight wrestling before. He expects people to be shocked.
Why it matters: Pettis is a big underdog by his own admission, and he is betting that a style nobody has seen from him can upset one of the sport's most in-form wrestlers.

h: Fury Cleared By Boxing Board For Joshua Fight, Davies Says
sum: Journalist Gareth A. Davies says the board cleared Fury's medicals after mental health headlines, so the December 11 fight against Joshua is on.
q: there is not an issue around his mental health right now in order for him to progress and fight Anthony Joshua on December the 11th
ctx: Interview on iFL TV
body: Davies says he spoke to the boxing board and was told Fury cleared his medicals on Thursday night. He says the promoter was informed on Friday morning.

The questions came after a Netflix documentary and its press release, which carried comments from Paris Fury about his mental health. Davies says the release quoted her describing mild schizophrenia, but that Fury was never diagnosed with it. He says Fury has had bouts of mania linked to bipolar disorder. He says the Fury camp asked Netflix to remove the scene.

Davies argues the story was blown out of proportion. He says the board was simply responding to the noise, and that the retrospective comments needed investigating. In his words, “this fight was never under threat” unless one of the fighters was unwell.

Why it matters: The clearance removes doubt over the biggest British heavyweight fight in years, two weeks before the bell. Fury is cleared to face Joshua in Cardiff, and the Joshua camp has stayed quiet on the matter.

h: Odiase Says Joshua Needs The Right Energy To Beat Fury
sum: Heavyweight Emanuel Odiase says Joshua must bring the right mindset against Fury, and calls the fight huge despite both being past their primes.
q: That legendary goat energy, bro. Then he can beat anyone.
ctx: Interview with Seconds Out ahead of his fight with Mike Perez
body: Heavyweight Emanuel Odiase, who says he fights Mike Perez tomorrow, was asked whether Anthony Joshua has to be like Muhammad Ali to beat Tyson Fury. His answer was about mindset. Joshua needs the right energy, and with it Odiase believes he can beat anyone.

He then dropped the jokes and said Joshua has to arrive in the right frame of mind. “AJ's got to come with the right energy.” Odiase added that he thinks Joshua is doing exactly that, and hopes both men come in at their best.
Earlier in the interview, Odiase said Fury and Joshua waited a long time to fight. In his view, both are past their primes. He still believes the fight is a big one.
Why it matters: Fury and Joshua meet on December 11, and a rising heavyweight is telling fans the outcome could come down to Joshua's mindset rather than just skills.

h: Kraus Says Whitaker Isn't Ready And Vows To Knock Him Out
sum: Gradus Kraus says he would stop Ben Whitaker if they met, picks Bivol to beat Callum Smith, and wants a world title shot next year.
q: for 12 rounds I think Whitaker is not ready yet and for sure not when he is with me in the ring.
ctx: Interview with Seconds Out, the day before his fight
body: Gradus Kraus was asked if he would fight Ben Whitaker next. He said yes and promised a stoppage: “I will knock him out”. He says his pressure and power are better than what Whitaker faced in his last fight, and that Whitaker doesn't like pressure.
Kraus gave Whitaker credit for his early work. He called him fast, with good distance, and sharp. But he pointed to the closing rounds of Whitaker's last fight and said it is over when it is over.

Kraus also said he is ready for his fight tomorrow night against Adam Deans and that Deans is going to feel “real power”. He wants a world title fight, hopes it comes next year, and says he would stop both Willie Hutchinson and Joshua Buatsi in one night. On Bivol, he picks him to beat Callum Smith but says he would pressure Bivol and land his heavy punches.
Why it matters: Kraus is calling out Whitaker and a world title shot in the same interview. A win tomorrow night would give those calls more weight.

h: Brown Open To Moving Cordina Higher On Fury-Joshua Undercard
sum: After Eddie Hearn's gripe over Joe Cordina's slot, Spencer Brown says the Welshman's placement may change. He also defends the undercard as Netflix-driven.
q: I think Joe deserves to be right at the top of the card
ctx: Interview with Seconds Out
body: Spencer Brown says Joe Cordina's spot on the Fury vs Joshua undercard could be changed. Asked about Eddie Hearn's complaint over where Cordina sits, Brown said it is something they will look at to see if they can move him up the card.
Brown said Cordina is a local Cardiff lad whom everybody was crying out for, and gave Hearn credit for getting him on the show. He also argued Cordina belongs at the top of the undercard.

He defended the undercard overall, pointing to Netflix's global audience and the need for international fighters. On who controls the card, he was blunt: “They're paying for it.” He said they will push to get Cordina further up but can only do what they can.
Why it matters: British fans have grumbled about the undercard, and Cordina's placement is the clearest flashpoint. Nothing is confirmed, but Brown has left the door open to a change.

h: Shalom Vows To Enforce Contract Over Bakole's Wilder Fight
sum: Ben Shalom calls the Bakole situation a mess and says he will enforce his contractual rights, with a week or two of drama ahead.
q: Look, we will uh we will enforce our contractual rights and that's it.
ctx: Interview with Seconds Out in Amsterdam
body: Promoter Ben Shalom says he will go by the letter of the contract with Martin Bakole. Bakole has been announced as Deontay Wilder's new opponent, replacing Opetaia.

Shalom says he doesn't know why whoever advises the fighter doesn't just say to “sort out the mess first”. He says his side are reasonable people and things can be sorted. But he can't tell his staff, lawyers and finance people not to enforce a contract, and says the situation has put them in a position where they have to. He called it a shame for the fighter, adding “it always ends in tears”.

He also aimed at Zuffa. He said he couldn't believe a British fighter wasn't offered the chance, and that Zuffa's fingerprints were all over the undercard. He said the whole thing is a mess and that it comes down to Zuffa. He expects a very interesting week or two.
Why it matters: if Shalom follows through, Bakole's place opposite Wilder on the Fury-Joshua bill could be in doubt just as the card is being finalised.

h: Atlas Says Hysa Won't Last The Night Against Kabayel
sum: Teddy Atlas sees Hysa's right hand as his only real chance and expects Kabayel's pressure to end it early in Germany.
q: he is going from the waiting pool to the ocean. And he'll probably get drowned.
ctx: Fight preview on THE FIGHT with Teddy Atlas
body: Teddy Atlas previewed WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel's defense against Nelson Hysa in Germany and picked the champion to stop him. The show described Hysa as 25-0 with 23 knockouts and 42 years old. It said he turned pro at 37 and is an 18-1 underdog.

Atlas says Hysa's one path to an upset is the right hand. He admits he doesn't know how much power it carries, because the opponents it has knocked out have not been high level. In his words, “I just don't know how hard he punches with the right hand.” He argues the jump in competition will be too big for the Albanian.

On Kabayel, Atlas praises a relentless, thick-boned pressure fighter with a good chin and a strong body attack, and he compares him to Daniel Dubois. He does see a flaw. Kabayel can get anxious for the knockout and take extra shots, especially uppercuts, and a straight right can catch him if he jabs from too close.
Atlas says he doesn't see Hysa lasting the whole night. He is leaning toward a no on the fight going the distance once the props are posted. His official pick is reserved for his subscription site.

Why it matters: A respected voice expects an early finish for the champion, while Hysa's backers are hoping for an upset. Atlas's one caveat is that nobody knows how hard Hysa's right hand really lands against a heavyweight of this level.

h: Hearn Says Fury And Joshua Will Punch For Ringwalk Order
sum: Eddie Hearn says a signed contract addendum has Fury and Joshua hitting a punch machine in fight week, with the top score walking second.
q: there will be a punch machine on fight week that both fighters will punch and the biggest score, the highest score will walk second.
ctx: Interview clip released by Matchroom Boxing
body: Eddie Hearn says the order of the Fury vs Joshua ringwalks will be settled by a contest. A punch machine will be set up in fight week, and both fighters will take a shot at it.
The fighter who posts the highest score will walk second. Hearn says the arrangement is part of the most recent contract, in an addendum. He says Netflix apparently likes the idea too.
Hearn stressed it is official, calling it “signed and papered.” He also appeared to suggest Tyson Fury may not want to play along, but said “it's in our contract.”
Why it matters: ringwalk order is usually a status issue between two big names, and here it comes down to a contractual punching contest in fight week, ahead of the December 11 fight.

h: Spencer Brown Says Fury Fight Is On Despite Health Claims
sum: Spencer Brown says there is no diagnosis behind the schizophrenia reports, that Fury is in great spirits, and that the Joshua fight is happening.
q: there's no way in the world that Tyson Fury was schizophrenic
ctx: Interview with iFL TV
body: Spencer Brown shot down recent reports about Tyson Fury's mental health. He said there is no diagnosis, that the issue is historical, and that it resurfaced because of a comment in a documentary segment that he says was never due to air.

Brown called the coverage sensationalism and said Fury has been open about his mental health struggles and should be praised for it, not criticised. He said the boxing board has cleared Fury to fight and that there was never any doubt about it.

He also said Anthony Joshua's side got in touch to ask if Fury was all right and if the fight was still on. Brown's answer: “The fight's on.” He said he speaks to Fury every day, that Fury is in the best headspace he has seen him in, and that he arrives in England next week.
Why it matters: With the fight two weeks away, the headlines had raised questions about whether it would go ahead. Brown's camp is now saying it will, and that Fury is fit to fight.

h: Napper Says Eubank Jr vs Brook Decision Due In Days
sum: Eubank Jr's manager says a decision on a Kell Brook fight is coming within days. He also gave the likely weight, location and timing.
q: It's closer than it's ever been ever before.
who: Napper, manager of Chris Eubank Jr
ctx: Interview with Boxing King Media in Dubai
body: Napper says talks for Chris Eubank Jr vs Kell Brook are further along than at any earlier point. He says the camp is “more hot than cold”. A decision on whether the fight happens should come in the next couple of days, though he wouldn't say when an announcement might follow.

He says the team is trying to get a few things over the line. If they do, there's a fight. If they don't, there isn't. He wouldn't say who would promote it, noting that Eubank Jr is a free agent who can work with whoever offers the most.

On the details, Napper says it would be at super middleweight with no weight clauses on either fighter. The location would probably be the UK, and the timing is “First quarter of next year.” He says Eubank Jr has long been up for the fight and has wanted it since Brook beat Khan.

Why it matters: A Eubank Jr vs Brook fight would be a big domestic night in the UK, and Napper says any other names linked to Eubank Jr, including Conor Benn, are off the table until this one is settled.

h: Kape Tells Van His Title Reign Ends In Toronto
sum: Manel Kape says he's on another level from champion Joshua Van and predicts a body-head attack that ends with Van dropped in Toronto.
q: You cannot compare me and him. This is this is a big insult.
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting
body: Manel Kape says flyweight champion Joshua Van's time is up. Speaking to MMA Fighting before their UFC 336 fight in Toronto, Kape said he has no hard feelings and isn't underestimating Van. But he called this "the end of the road" and said the belt is going home with him.

Kape said he was more impressed by how Pantoja fought than by Van's performance. He said Pantoja was emotional in that fight and paid the price. He gave Van credit for maturity on the ground, but he dismissed his striking as that of a regular fighter and said they are in different levels.

He was blunt about the gap. Kape said “whatever Joshua Van do, I do I do 10 times better.” As for how it ends, he predicts a body-head attack that wears Van down, followed by a finish. In his words, he'll “drop him like I drop everyone.”
Why it matters: Kape has waited a long time for this title shot and is selling it as a changing of the guard. His confidence adds some edge to a flyweight title fight that is usually respectful.

h: Haney Camp Stops Pushing Voluntary Testing Before December 19 Fight
sum: Someone speaking for Devin Haney's camp says they won't be pushed into extra VADA testing, insisting the December 19 fight was signed under existing rules.
q: If you really trying to volunteer and show the people, then do it the right way.
who: Speaker from Devin Haney's camp (not named in the video)
ctx: Video shared by FightHype, first sighting of Haney since the VADA testing drama
body: A member of Devin Haney's camp, who isn't named in the video, says Haney is the most tested athlete in boxing and has volunteered for testing more than anyone. The speaker says the camp signed up for the program when nobody else would, and that people laughed at them for it.

The camp is now backing away from that stance. The speaker says they are comfortable with WBO, IBF and California State Athletic Commission testing, but “I'm no longer encouraging Devin to volunteer”. The speaker also says other fighters didn't volunteer before their own fights.

On the December 19 fight, the speaker says it was signed under the same conditions and championship rules as the last one, and that the other side can't get out of it. Asking Haney to volunteer now, the speaker says, is something “we don't have to volunteer”, and the camp objects to the request coming in the 11th hour.

Why it matters: The testing dispute is now a public fight between the two camps weeks before the December 19 date. The speaker's message is that Haney will fight under the existing rules and won't take extra voluntary testing.

h: Kabayel Says He Feels No Pressure As Favorite Against Hysa
sum: The WBC champion says the role reversal from underdog to favorite doesn't weigh on him as he heads into Saturday's title defense.
q: there's no pressure for me, I'm the favorite right now.
ctx: Final press conference
body: Asked whether he feels more pressure now that everyone expects him to win, Kabayel said the situation has flipped. He pointed out that he was repeatedly cast as the underdog earlier in his run, and that he is now the favorite.
He said that isn't a burden. His focus is on improving from fight to fight, and he said he wants to show people that “I want to be better in every fight”.
Kabayel also called Saturday the start of a new era for him. He said Tyson Fury's win over Vladimir Klitschko 11 years ago inspired him, and that he now shares a manager with Fury.

Why it matters: Kabayel is heading into a 12-round WBC title defense in front of a huge crowd against an unbeaten challenger. His calm tone suggests he isn't feeling the weight of the favorite's role.

h: Richman Believes He Can Put Pague Away In Hershey Main Event
sum: Mike Richman says he can stop BKFC champion Dustin Pague on December 4 and explains why the 168-pound catchweight fight matters to his title hopes.
q: I think I can put him away, but I it's nothing against Dustin. I think I can knock out anybody.
ctx: Interview on The Mike & Mish Show
body: Mike Richman says he sees a knockout as a real possibility against Dustin Pague, though he admits the fight could go to a decision. If it does, he says it comes down to who landed the most power and did the most damage.

Richman says Pague is really good at range with a long jab and long hooks. His plan is to get inside, make it dirty and hit him hard. He also stressed that he respects Pague, calling him an OG, and expects the two to embrace after trying to knock each other out.

He explained that the fight is at a 168-pound catchweight because Pague didn't want to fight at 175 and Richman hasn't fought at 165 yet. He says a win keeps him in the mix at a high level, and that he told the promotion “I'll fight any top dude at 65, 75, or 85.”

Why it matters: Beating the 165-pound champion would throw the division's pecking order into question, and Richman says the promotion would have to figure out what comes next. It also makes the December 4 main event a real test of his push to stay near the top.

h: Alvey Predicts BKFC Title By July 2027 After Hershey Debut
sum: Sam Alvey wants a knockout in his bare knuckle debut against Jonathan Miller and says the BKFC belt will be his within months.
q: I want to win. I want to get in there and I want to floor him.
ctx: Interview on Bare Knuckle Bowker ahead of BKFC Hershey
body: Sam Alvey makes his bare knuckle debut against Jonathan Miller in the co-main event of BKFC Hershey on December 4. He says a win isn't enough. He wants a knockout and wants to be talked about like Mike Perry, and he wants to be the rising star of the league.

Alvey says he is a prize fighter and BKFC offered a big prize. He gave himself a timeline for the belt, saying “I think by July of 2027 I will be the BKFC champion.” He also said it won't happen in the first fight, but shortly after.

He called Miller a game opponent who throws hard and fast, and said he has been training to match that pace. Asked about iron weight champion Lorenzo Hunt, he called him a stud and said he is looking forward to getting his hand raised after fighting him. Alvey also revived an old callout of Darren Till, saying “I've always wanted to fight Darren Till, too.” He said he would make his way down to 205 if Till wants it.

Why it matters: Alvey is a veteran stepping into a fresh iron weight division and already naming the champion and a marquee name as targets. A strong debut against Miller would test whether the talk holds up.

h: Hysa Vows To Beat Kabayel And Host Rematch In Albania
sum: Challenger Nelson Hysa says he's fully prepared, expects to win the WBC title, and is already planning the rematch at home. He also took a swipe at Kabayel's hands.
q: So after we will win the match the other match the rematch will be in Albania.
ctx: Official press conference in Dusseldorf
body: Nelson Hysa used the Dusseldorf press conference to say he's ready for Agit Kabayel's WBC heavyweight title on Saturday. He said training camp went well and his team is fully prepared. He called himself realistic, then looked past the fight to a rematch he expects to stage in Albania.
He invited everyone in the room to come to Albania and see the country. The fight falls on Albanian National Day, as the host pointed out.

Asked about game plans, Hysa said nobody gives theirs away. The host relayed that Kabayel wouldn't reveal his either, and joked that Kabayel's coach already had his hands in an ice bucket. Hysa turned the joke around: “But I think Agit will have problem with hands.”

Why it matters: Hysa is the challenger, and he's talking about winning and a return bout at home, not just turning up. With a sold-out crowd expected in Germany, he's telling the champion he won't be intimidated.

h: Hysa Won't Say Knockout But Hints At One Against Kabayel
sum: Fight week in Düsseldorf: Hysa calls Kabayel a tough, top-level champion, then points to his knockout record and says he has nothing to defend.
q: Listen, I will not say knock out or not, but I will say that I will improve my 92% of KO.
ctx: Fight week interview with iFL TV in Düsseldorf
body: Nelson Hysa is at the start of fight week for his WBC heavyweight title shot against Agit Kabayel in Düsseldorf. He says camp was the best of his life and that he is "more than ready".

Pushed on whether he is predicting a knockout, Hysa wouldn't say so directly. He pointed to his 92% knockout rate instead, and the interviewer noted he was hinting at one anyway. He was respectful of Kabayel, calling him a tough opponent and a top guy, but he doesn't rate him above the other heavyweight champions. His message for the champion was a cheeky one: “brother don't be sad when I win the match”.

Hysa is fighting in Kabayel's home country, but he expects the crowd to be split about 50-50 because of the number of Albanians travelling. He shrugged off the underdog label. “I don't have nothing to defend”, he said, and he believes the pressure sits on the champion.
Why it matters: Hysa is chasing the first world heavyweight title for an Albanian flag, and he is laying out a clear plan to take the belt in Kabayel's backyard.

h: Overeem Gives Verhoeven Until 2027 To Accept A Fight
sum: Ahead of his Dec. 24 boxing return against Manuwa, Overeem says Verhoeven ignored his challenge and vows to knock him out too.
q: By 2027 either I have fought Rico Verhoeven or the whole world will know he does not want to face me.
ctx: Interview with Seconds Out
body: Alistair Overeem is back in camp for his boxing bout with Jimi Manuwa on Dec. 24 in Dubai, and he is already looking past it. He says his team pushed for a fight with Rico Verhoeven and never got an answer.

Overeem says he thinks Verhoeven believes he is above the fight: “I think he thinks he's above me or something.” He called himself a patient man and says the plan is simple: “we're going to knock out Jimmy and then we're going to go right back to Rico”.

He also predicted that Manuwa will be finished and that he would knock out Verhoeven as well if they fight. He named Francis Ngannou and other big boxing names as options, but said he won't chase Verhoeven. If it happens, he wants it in the Netherlands. Asked about Fury vs Joshua, he leans towards Joshua, citing mental strength.

Why it matters: Overeem has put a deadline on a kickboxing-versus-boxing grudge, and everything depends on him beating Manuwa first. If he does, the Verhoeven callout will be hard for either side to ignore.

h: Thurman Starts Rehab After Ortiz Pullout, Vows He's Not Done
sum: Keith Thurman breaks his silence after pulling out of the Vergil Ortiz fight. He says he is in rehab, aiming for 2027, and not ready to retire.
q: it's not over. I'm not ready to hang the gloves up quite yet. So, I'm going to keep milking the cow and squeezing the juice out of this game.
ctx: Rehab video message and interview with FightHype
body: Keith Thurman has spoken for the first time since pulling out of his fight with Vergil Ortiz. He opened with a clip from a physical therapy session, calling it day one of getting back right in rehab. He wished fans a happy Thanksgiving and said he plans to return ready and strong in 2027.

In the interview, Thurman said he feels like he is making up for lost time. He said this is statistically the first year since 2019 that he fought twice, and admitted “I just feel like I'm playing catch-up.” He tried to stay positive, saying “I'm happy to be here.”

He blamed much of his long inactivity on industry politics and network shifts. After beating Mario Barrios, he said, Barrios ended up facing Ugas instead of him, which left him on the sidelines. He later got a headline slot against Tim Tszyu, but popped his bicep tendon two weeks before the fight. That added another year out of the ring.
Why it matters: Thurman's withdrawal from the Ortiz fight leaves him on the shelf again, but he is making clear he has no plans to retire. A return is not expected before 2027.

h: Dubois Says He'll Take On Kabayel And Wants Back On Top
sum: Asked about a possible fight with Agit Kabayel, Daniel Dubois says he's fit and ready. Kabayel says he'll face anyone after his Nov 28 fight with Nelson Hysa.
q: I'm ready for him, you know. I'm ready to get back to the top.
ctx: Interview segment with DAZN Boxing ahead of Kabayel vs Hysa
body: Daniel Dubois has said he is willing to fight Agit Kabayel. The host asked him about the talk of a Dubois-Kabayel matchup, and Dubois said he is fit and ready to go and will take it on.

Kabayel spoke first. He said he fights in Germany and can face other opponents after that, and that he sees only the sporting competition. He has no personal problem with the other fighters and said “I'm ready for everyone.”
The host called the matchup a fantastic one for the future. Dubois was asked how it would go and gave no game plan, only saying he is ready for Kabayel and wants to get back to the top.
Why it matters: Kabayel faces Nelson Hysa on Nov 28, and the video title says a win could set up a Dubois fight next year. With Dubois now saying he'll take it, the talk has a second name behind it.

h: Hysa Admits Kabayel Is No Rabbit Before Title Fight
sum: Nelson Hysa takes back his taunts about Agit Kabayel and explains why he confronted him at ringside. He also says the key to winning is to keep smiling.
q: I know that he's not a rabbit. He's a good boxer. He's a tough fighter.
ctx: Fight week interview with Queensberry Promotions
body: Hysa had earlier called Kabayel a rabbit and said he was running from him. In fight week he says that's over. He told the interviewer Kabayel is no longer running and that the fight is happening.

He says the taunts came from frustration. He claims he had been trying to make a big fight in Germany, and the other camp said no. After he climbed out of the ring and confronted Kabayel at ringside, he says he wasn't getting the answer he wanted on a contract. Now he says he has big respect for what Kabayel has done in his career.

Asked for the key to victory, Hysa wouldn't give up the tactics. His answer was “the key is the smile. Always smile.” He says he'll keep smiling until he steps through the ropes, then get serious. He says he feels no pressure to stop Kabayel, and he is in Dusseldorf to take the WBC belt.

Why it matters: The hostility behind this fight has cooled into mutual respect, but Hysa's message is still clear. He sees himself as the man who made this fight happen, and he says he has come to Germany to win the title.

h: Mendoza Accepts Ortiz Fight, Vows To Deliver Next Big Upset
sum: Brian Mendoza says he has taken the Vergil Ortiz Jr. fight on Dec. 5 in Phoenix and wants to close out 2026 with an upset.
q: Let's close out 2026 with the next big upset.
ctx: Video message posted by Premier Boxing Champions
body: Brian Mendoza says he has taken the fight against Vergil Ortiz Jr. on December 5 in Phoenix. He says the news is already out, and he sounds eager to get going.
Mendoza is confident. He says he is “I'm born for this” material and can't wait for the opportunity. He wants to be ready for it.
He also frames the fight as a chance to pull off the next big upset. The card is listed as a pay-per-view on DAZN and Prime Video.
Why it matters: Ortiz vs. Mendoza is not yet on our schedule. Mendoza is openly casting himself as the one who can spoil Ortiz's night.

h: Woodley Wants Chimaev Rematch And One More MMA Fight
sum: Woodley says the Chimaev loss still eats at him, he wants it run back, and he believes he has one more MMA fight left.
q: I feel like I got at least one more MMA fight before I hang that up
ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting's Mike Heck
body: Tyron Woodley says he wants to run back his loss to Khamzat Chimaev. Asked about it, he said he “definitely want to run that one back” and admitted the defeat is still on his mind. He says he has told his promoters he wants a rematch and is willing to earn it with other fights first.

Woodley blames himself for the loss, not Chimaev. He says his camp and weight cut went perfectly, but a message he read in the locker room about an hour before the walkout threw him off. He says he fought the opposite of his game plan, and he has not asked for a rematch against anyone else he has lost to.

He also addressed his future. Woodley says he has not fought MMA since 2021 and has never officially retired. He wants one more MMA fight and says new breathing and focus work has changed his approach. He said a big match was offered and he accepted, but his opponent had not yet accepted. He also said “I'm not the last minute opponent” and that January is the earliest he can compete.
Why it matters: Woodley is putting a rematch with Chimaev and a return to MMA on the table. No date or opponent is set, so it stays talk for now, but he is clearly not done.

h: Prates Vows To Hit Makhachev So Hard He Never Fights Again
sum: Carlos Prates is already looking past Morales and promises a Makhachev fight that ends with Makhachev wanting out of the sport.
q: when I meet him inside the octagon, I'm going to hit him so hard, he's going to think like, oh my god, I'm never going to fight again.
ctx: Interview clip from The MMA Hour
body: Carlos Prates has made his next two targets clear. He says his focus right now is Morales, and he expects to get past him before turning to Islam Makhachev.
Prates did not leave the Makhachev plan vague. He promised that when the two meet in the octagon, he will land something so heavy that Makhachev will question whether he ever wants to fight again.
His line is “Now my focus is Morales.” He sounds confident that the Morales fight is a stepping stone, not an obstacle.

Why it matters: Prates is publicly putting Makhachev in his sights and staking his next move on beating Morales first. No fight between Prates and Makhachev is booked, so this is a callout, not an announcement.

h: Borralho Wants Du Plessis Next And Says He Can Knock Him Out
sum: Borralho names Dricus du Plessis as his top target for a spring return and floats an interim belt to unclog the middleweight division.
q: I think the styles match very good and I think I can knock him out.
ctx: Interview on The Ariel Helwani Show
body: Fresh off his UFC 334 decision win over Yousri Belgaroui, Caio Borralho says he wants a high-ranked opponent next, someone from the top five or even the top 10. He is targeting a return in late February or March. He named Brendan Allen, Dricus du Plessis and Khamzat Chimaev as fights that make sense.

Asked to pick one, he didn't hesitate: “Dricus is my preference.” He says he has called out Du Plessis in his post-fight interviews several times. He admits Du Plessis has said he has an announcement coming, and that it's "definitely not me."

Borralho also weighed in on the log jam caused by Sean Strickland's contract dispute and Imavov's long wait for a title shot. He feels for Imavov and thinks the UFC may soon create an interim belt, as it did at welterweight. If Strickland and Imavov do fight, he says “I think Imavov gets this one,” though only at around 55-45, maybe 50-50.
Why it matters: Middleweight is stuck while the title picture waits on Strickland's deal. Borralho is pushing for a marquee name and hinting the UFC could break the stall with an interim title.

h: Hooker Wants Bobby Green In Sydney After Ortega Win
sum: Fresh off beating Ortega, Hooker says he wants a quick turnaround against Green in Sydney. He'd also fight Moicano, and he needs hand surgery.
q: If it was up to me, I would like that fight in in Sydney.
ctx: Interview on The Ariel Helwani Show
body: Dan Hooker is already looking for his next fight after beating Brian Ortega at UFC Qatar. He told Ariel Helwani he asked for Bobby Green in Sydney before the fight, but it looks like the UFC doesn't want to give him anyone old.

Helwani said the UFC appeared to have turned down a Max Holloway fight. Hooker shrugged it off and said the promotion will do what it does and probably match him with a young, hungry killer. He picked Green over Renato Moicano because “Green's actually going to fight me.” He joked that “Uncle needs the cash.”

Hooker is also happy to fight Moicano and said he's down for it. He added that he has hate left in him: “There is still deep-seated hatred in my heart, and I love inflicting damage more than I love to do anything.” He said he needs a procedure to shave bone from a hand he broke a couple of years ago so he can make a fist, but that he can still fight with it.

Why it matters: Hooker has snapped his skid and wants to stay busy, but the UFC hasn't offered him a fight. A Sydney bout with Green looks like his preferred next step, and the hand surgery could affect when he fights.

h: Hokit Fires Back At Jon Jones, Says Diss Track Is Done
sum: Josh Hokit says he got the better of Jon Jones in sparring, calls him a "clout demon" and reveals he has finished a diss track.
q: Man, he's just a clout demon, man. You see where his mind's at.
ctx: Interview on The MMA Hour with Ariel Helwani
body: Josh Hokit was asked what happens if he runs into Jon Jones in Albuquerque. He answered with a hard-edged warning and said there are "certain things he has to pay for."

Hokit said his anger comes from what he describes as the fallout for a former teammate who went to help with Jones's camp. In his words, living a certain way is one thing, but bringing others down with you is what bothers him.

He also looked back at sparring Jones early in his own career. Hokit claims he got the better of those rounds and that Jones was upset he was even hanging with him. "He knows where he can find me," he said.
Hokit then said he has finished a diss track and offered a few lines for Helwani, including "PED Jones a cheater." These are Hokit's own claims and insults.
Why it matters: No fight is booked between them, but Hokit's challenge adds a personal edge to any future meeting and shows he is willing to keep the feud going publicly.

h: Mesquita Vows To Finish Perez But Wants Peña First
sum: The UFC 334 winner says Perez isn't on her level and wants to finish her, but names Peña as the next fight on her road to a 2027 title.
q: I want to go out there, face her, finish her, and prove it that we don't need to be talking so many bad things
ctx: Interview on The Ariel Helwani Show
body: Fresh off her first-round submission at UFC 334, Bia Mesquita confirmed she doesn't like Ailin Perez. She said she dislikes how Perez acts in the media and called her shaking her backside in an opponent's face disrespectful and classless. She wants to answer by finishing her.

Asked if Perez is on her level as an athlete, Mesquita said she doesn't think so. She pointed to Perez's last fight as one the fans didn't want to watch. Even so, she says Juliana Peña is the name she wants next, as the bigger challenge on the way to the title. She said the UFC hasn't talked to her about it yet, but her team is working on it.

On a possible fight with teammate Kayla Harrison, Mesquita hopes Harrison moves up to 145 for an Amanda Nunes rematch and leaves the 135-pound crown behind. If the UFC did ask, she said, “I would say yes, of course”. She also said the fight would stay professional. She also told the story of giving streamer Clavicular her number out of curiosity, and says she felt disrespected once she saw his videos.
Why it matters: Mesquita is openly targeting a 2027 title shot at 135 pounds. Her choice of Peña over Perez shows how she wants to get there, even with bad blood building with Perez.

h: Prates Predicts Three Rounds And Questions Morales' Striking
sum: Prates calls Morales strong but unproven against technical strikers and doubts his cardio ahead of their interim welterweight title fight on January 30.
q: But when he got like somebody like really good to strike, like know how to move, how to defense, it's going to be hard.
ctx: Interview on The Ariel Helwani Show
body: Carlos Prates expects his interim title fight with Michael Morales to end early. Asked how long it lasts, he said maybe three rounds, and he doesn't see it going the distance.

He named striking as the area where Morales is lacking. Prates described him as a big, strong fighter who walks forward and throws, and said that could be a problem against someone who moves and defends well. He gave Morales credit as a good wrestler because of his size and strength.

Prates also raised Morales' cardio and the weight he cuts. He said “I don't think the fight going to be five rounds” and added that he can go five, seven or eight rounds himself. On whether Morales has earned this spot, he said “I think he did enough to fight against me for interim title.” He doesn't think Morales has done enough to fight Makhachev.
Why it matters: Prates has laid out his game plan for the January 30 fight. Winning it is also his route back to the Makhachev fight he lost when Makhachev backed out of January.

h: Bakole Steps In For Injured Opetaia To Face Wilder
sum: The Cardiff co-main event has a new look less than three weeks out, and Wilder’s night just got a lot heavier.
body: Jai Opetaia is out of his heavyweight debut against Deontay Wilder after aggravating a hand injury in camp. Martin Bakole (22-2-1, 16 KOs) takes his place in the co-main event of Fury vs Joshua on December 11, and the swap was made official on Monday.
It changes the fight completely. Instead of a smaller, faster cruiserweight, Wilder now faces a genuine heavyweight with real power.

Bakole’s last short-notice call did not go well. He came in out of shape against Joseph Parker and was stopped in the second round, then needed a fortunate draw against Efe Ajagba. He hasn’t fought in about 18 months.
Why it matters: Wilder has looked like a fading force since his trilogy with Fury ended in 2021. A win keeps him relevant at heavyweight. A loss to a rusty Bakole could end the conversation.

h: Fury Promises Joshua Won’t Hear The Final Bell
sum: At the launch press conference, Fury said he’s done boxing clever. He’s coming to knock Joshua out.
q: I’m gonna catch him, and when I do, it’s gonna be curtains.
ctx: Fury vs Joshua launch press conference
body: Tyson Fury didn’t wait for fight week to make his prediction. At the London launch press conference for their December 11 fight in Cardiff, he laid out the whole plan: a fast start, no running, no boxing, just a straight fight he compared to the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

Joshua didn’t flinch. He said Fury’s knockout talk is exactly the energy he wants, and it’s what will push him through the extra rounds in the gym. When Fury joked that Joshua was built like a marble statue but couldn’t take a shot, Joshua laughed it off: “That’s also true.”
Why it matters: Fury is 38 and Joshua turns 37 before fight night. After a decade of failed talks, this is the fight both men will be remembered for.

h: Lopes Moves Up And Asks Oliveira For A War
sum: His first fight at 155 is for the BMF belt, and he has zero interest in playing it safe.
q: I want to get in there and throw down. Let’s see who goes down first.
ctx: On his UFC 335 BMF title fight
body: Diego Lopes is skipping the warm-up. The two-time featherweight title challenger makes his lightweight debut in the UFC 335 main event against Charles Oliveira on December 12, with the BMF belt on the line.

He says he respects Oliveira, but believes his all-action style is what the BMF title is supposed to be about. He wants to stand in the pocket with one of the most dangerous finishers the UFC has ever had.
Dana White is already bracing for it, calling the matchup “absolutely bat s*** crazy.”
Why it matters: Oliveira and Lopes have 56 professional finishes between them. Neither man knows how to have a boring fight.

h: Benavidez Says Cieślak Is The Last Step Before Something Bigger
sum: The unbeaten champion comes home to Arizona with three belts on the line and his eyes on a much bigger name.
q: I’m the best fighter in all of boxing, but I have to prove it.
ctx: Benavidez vs Cieślak kickoff press conference
body: David Benavidez insists he isn’t looking past Michał Cieślak. Thirteen weeks into camp, he says his focus is fully on the Polish WBC champion, who he meets on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona.
He called his last fight probably the best performance of his career, and says beating Cieślak would make him the king of the cruiserweight division.
Cieślak isn’t intimidated. He watched Benavidez beat Zurdo Ramírez, thought he fought pretty well, and says December 5 will show Benavidez what he should have done better.
Why it matters: Benavidez calls this the last thing standing in the way of an even bigger fight, and he’s been open in recent interviews about wanting Oleksandr Usyk next.

h: Joshua Isn’t Buying Fury’s Nice-Guy Act
sum: Fury praised AJ and offered him a post-fight pint. Joshua smiled and kept his guard up.
q: I don’t know if I can trust you.
ctx: Replying to Fury’s post-fight Guinness invite
body: The launch press conference was friendlier than anyone expected. Fury called Joshua a role model for British boxing, said he even defends him to fans he meets in the street, and suggested they go for a pint of Guinness once the fighting is done.
Joshua wasn’t biting. Fury has played mind games before big fights for years, and AJ answered the invite with a smile and a warning.
The face-off ended with Joshua tickling Fury in the stomach, the strangest moment of a strange afternoon.
Why it matters: A friendly Fury can be the most dangerous Fury. Joshua is making it clear he won’t be talked into relaxing.

h: Oliveira Says He’s Next In Line For The Lightweight Title
sum: The BMF champion has a plan for 2027, and it starts with getting through Lopes.
q: If he retires, then it’s me and Arman fighting for the vacant title.
ctx: On the lightweight title picture
body: Charles Oliveira took the BMF belt from Max Holloway at UFC 326. Now he defends it against Diego Lopes, but the belt he really wants is the one he used to hold.
Asked whether winning the UFC lightweight title again before he retires still matters to him, Oliveira kept it short: “That’s my dream.”
He says everyone knows he’s a problem for the division and that he’s next. First, he wants the UFC to find out what Justin Gaethje plans to do.
Why it matters: If Gaethje steps away, Oliveira sees a vacant-title fight with Arman Tsarukyan. A loss to Lopes would wipe that plan out.

h: Cieślak Plans To Take All Three Belts Back To Poland
sum: The away fighter in Glendale isn’t treating this as a trip to lose.
q: I will bring all three belts back to Poland after December 5.
ctx: After the fight was announced
body: Michał Cieślak holds the WBC cruiserweight title and walks into Benavidez’s home crowd in Glendale, Arizona, on December 5. The WBA and WBO belts are on the line too.
He doesn’t sound worried about the crowd or the favorite. Cieślak has studied Benavidez’s recent work and believes he can expose what Benavidez didn’t do well.
Why it matters: Most expect a Benavidez win. An upset would blow up the cruiserweight division and every big plan Benavidez has for 2027.

h: Joshua On Fury Fight: ‘No Better Time Than Now’
sum: After years of failed talks, AJ sounds like a man who’s just glad it’s finally real.
q: It had to happen at some stage and there’s no better time than now.
ctx: Fury vs Joshua launch press conference
body: Fury and Joshua first shared a ring in a 2010 sparring session, when Fury was an up-and-coming pro and Joshua was still an amateur. Fans have wanted the real thing for most of the years since.
Joshua says he knows people have argued about this fight in pubs, and that family members have fallen out over who wins. He says he’s just happy to be fighting and fulfilling his destiny.
Why it matters: For years the fight felt like it would never happen. Now both men are talking like it’s the last big chapter of their careers.
